description: Phase 4B exploratory scripted pacing observation, not a golden baseline, acceptance threshold, human play sample, or HTTP/session validation.

profiles.seeded_coach: Equal 70-rated rosters; alternate inside_run/slant; punt/field goal on fourth; no penalties, injuries, timeouts, overtime.
profiles.scripted_physics: Actual fixed-tick physics recordings at actual LOS; two defenders; same intended 50/50 run/pass mix. Run straight with small initial lateral input and a tick38 juke. Pass at tick55 to alternating receiver plus four yards x, no z lead.
profiles.scripted_early_lead: Same physics run profile. Pass at tick30 to receiver with largest projected distance from defenders, 0.7s velocity lead in x and z.

limitations: Not actual human inputs or an assessment of full eleven-on-eleven football balance.
Physics outputs go directly to shared accounting/finalization in this accounting benchmark; HTTP persistence, contract validation and concurrency are separate tests.
Coach resolves only special teams in physics games, never a replacement for an interactive outcome.
Presentation omitted from finalization; full-game metrics do not retain replay history.
Counts are offensive run/pass snaps and offensive possessions, including a partial final possession; drive length is offensive snaps per possession.
Coach intended passes can end as tackle outcomes; rush/pass counts are play-call mix, not box-score classifications.
No acceptance threshold was fabricated: observed pace/possession disparity remains unresolved.
normal_120_conclusion: Matched outcome and duration isolation proves identical shared clock/accounting. Scripted physics profile does not establish comparable offensive pace: interceptions, touchdowns, incompletions and shorter live duration yield less average runoff and much shorter drives.

duration_only_clock_budget_estimate.scope: Analytical clock-budget estimate only, not human play or a replayed full simulation. Snaps-weighted 120-second normal-tempo observed live durations are substituted while holding runoff fixed. No changes to physics.
limitations: The 34-second case assumes every compared snap follows a running clock, so ignores start/stop events and boundaries.
The second case holds Coach observed average runoff fixed to isolate duration from the differing outcome mixes. It is an average-budget substitution, not a matched chronological outcome simulation.
Does not predict possessions, drive length, exact game snap count, touchdowns, or clock boundary effects. Special teams and first-snap/period effects are not modeled.
